title: Lake Ontario or Lake America? Tribal Leaders Say: Keep the Name
summary:
Lake Ontario has had its name for a very long time. The name comes from Indigenous languages. In Seneca, the lake is called sga:nyodai:yoh. It means 'beautiful lake.' In Wendat, it is called ontari:io. It means 'the lake is beautiful, the lake is big.'

In August, President Donald Trump told the federal government to start calling the lake Lake America. The National Congress of American Indians is asking him to undo that order. The group speaks for American Indian and Alaska Native tribal governments. It says the new name shows disrespect for Indigenous place names and for Indigenous ties to lands and waters.

In October, the group passed a resolution against the name change. The Seneca Nation of Indians, from western New York, put it forward. The resolution asks the U.S. government to stop using 'Lake America.' It also asks governments to respect Indigenous names, working with the Tribal Nations.

Wendat Grand Chief Pierre Picard said his nation was 'shocked' by the change. He called it an attempt to erase their history. Prime Minister Mark Carney has said the lake remains Lake Ontario 'then, now and always.'
why_it_matters: The names of lakes, rivers, and towns where you live can hold the history of the people who lived there first, so changing a name can feel like losing part of that story.
